chunks: 909 - And in another report, al-Sadiq عليه السلام said:

"A woman is not required to perform the adhan or the iqamah if she hears the adhan of the locality, and the two testimonies are sufficient for her. However, if she gives the adhan and the iqamah, then that is better.
And in the salat of the two Eids, there is no adhan and no iqamah; their adhan is the rising of the sun.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the call announcing the commencement of salat
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَانِ: the two testimonies, serving here as sufficient remembrance
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: a woman, in the context of prayer rulings
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the prayer of the two Eids
key_terms.طُلُوعُ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, indicating the time associated with Eid prayer

ai.seo_question: Is a woman required to give the adhan and iqamah, and is there an adhan for Eid prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about adhan and iqamah for women and for the salat of the two Eids. It states that a woman who hears the adhan of her locality is not obligated to give adhan or iqamah, though doing so is more virtuous, and it also states that the Eid prayer has neither adhan nor iqamah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.909 - In another report, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"A woman is not required to perform the adhan (call to prayer) or the iqamah (call to commence prayer) if She hears the adhan of her locality. The two testimonies (shahadatayn) are sufficient for her. However, if She chooses to give the adhan and iqamah, it is better."
